subject: Re: BluePeak - auditability & exportability Qs / next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Vivian Park <vivian.park@bluepeakhealth.com>, Paul Reyes <paul.reyes@bluepeakhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:23:00 -0800
Subject: BluePeak — quick recap from today’s security discovery call

Hi Vivian / Paul,

Thanks for taking the time today — good conversation. Below is a short recap plus proposed next steps so we’re aligned on what BluePeak needs from an auditability / logs perspective.

Recap (from our session)
- Primary use case: telemetry + security monitoring for LLM-backed workflows (PII tokenization checks, user-admin actions).
- Must-haves called out: admin activity logs (who changed model/config), API request logs (request IDs, timestamps, response codes, tokens-exchanged metadata), exportability to your SIEM, and immutable retention for compliance audits.
- Compliance context: BluePeak will need evidence for HIPAA readiness and wants to see recent SOC 2 artifacts before advancing the procurement path.

What Redwood can provide (high level)
- SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report (completed Sep 2025). We can share the report under NDA; summary attached.
- HIPAA / BAA: We support BAAs. For Hosted API customers we require a short security review; BAAs are available for Dedicated and Private deployments by default as part of the enterprise agreement.
- Logs: Admin activity logs and API logs are captured with request IDs, actor email, IP, timestamp, action, and object changed. Exports available in JSON/CSV; can be pushed to an S3 bucket (secure push) or delivered on-demand. Default retention is 90 days for Hosted, configurable to 1+ years on Dedicated/Private.
- Immutability: Dedicated and Private customers can enable append-only manifests with signed checkpoints and S3 WORM to meet tamper-evidence requirements. For Hosted we provide signed export manifests and a tamper-evident audit ledger for delivered exports.

Proposed next steps
1) I’ll drop our standard vendor security questionnaire link below for your team to start. Please complete the sections that are relevant and flag anything high risk.
2) Marissa (Product Security) and Karthik (Infra) to run a focused technical deep dive next week to demonstrate export flow and immutability options (30–45m). Suggested slots: Wed 11/18 or Thu 11/19.
3) If you want the SOC 2 Type II PDF we’ll send it once an NDA is in place.
4) I’ll prepare a short demo export (small subset) to your test S3 and a sample signed manifest.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary-202509.pdf, log-export-spec-1p0.docx

Thanks — I’ll take action on items 1 and 4 and coordinate scheduling.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivian Park <vivian.park@bluepeakhealth.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BluePeak — quick recap from today’s security discovery call

Hi Vivian,

Happy to jump in. Short answers and what we’ll demo in the deep dive: 

1) BAA coverage: Hosted customers can be covered by a BAA in specific conditions (data flow isolation, contract terms). For near-term procurement it’s often faster to evaluate Dedicated or Private if you need a standing BAA. We’ll include the BAA matrix in our follow-up packet.

2) Immutability guarantees (high level):
- Hosted: exports are delivered with cryptographic signatures and a tamper-evident export ledger (sequence of signed manifests). This satisfies many audit requirements where you need evidence that exported files haven’t been altered after delivery.
- Dedicated/Private: customers can enable write-once object locking (S3 WORM) and an append-only ledger under their control. For regulator-mandated immutability (e.g., retention holds), Dedicated is the recommended path.

3) Log schema & export mechanics: API logs include request_id, user_id (or service identity), endpoint, payload size, status_code, latency_ms, and a hashed token delta for debugging (no raw model tokens). Admin activity logs include actor_email, action_type, target_resource, before/after where applicable, and timestamp.

For the deep dive we’ll:
- Show a sample export to S3 (JSON + CSV examples),
- Walk through the signed manifest verification steps,
- Demonstrate how retention policies and WORM behave in Dedicated.

If you can share one or two sample retention & export requirements (e.g., 7 years / 1 month / immediate access), we’ll tailor the demo.

Thanks — looping Karthik to pick a time.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
